situation: An audio menu has two Spanish tracks, one commentary and one described. Product wants a badge on just the described one.
expected: Use the native description characteristic and independently identify both fixture options; leave the selected track alone.
decoy: Label every alternate-language track described.

situation: The menu highlights French but the same video keeps showing English captions. The player itself must not be replaced.
expected: Drive the installed picker setter and read the legible selection on that very item.
decoy: Assert that the menu's selected ID changed and stop there.

situation: A support screen says Ready whenever the buffer is full, including after the item failed.
expected: Expose buffer observations separately from player/item status; include contradictory states.
decoy: Treat a full buffer as proof playback will start.

situation: A user cancels a previous reload while the new reload is still showing progress.
expected: The old cancellation cannot reset the new owner's loading state; the current cancellation can.
decoy: Clear the single shared busy flag from any cancellation completion.

situation: A Favorite button shows a word in addition to its color. People can select and deselect it repeatedly.
expected: Update nonempty status and accessibility value consistently with the selected trait in both directions.
decoy: Test only the selected appearance on a fresh control.

situation: An invoice row has independently usable Open and Save controls. A grouped title should not replace either.
expected: Preserve two actual actionable children and current recipients; separate grouping from a single actionable parent.
decoy: Make the whole row one accessible item and assume its nested controls remain reachable.

situation: After a sort, the visual cards move but the list used for accessibility still has the old sequence.
expected: Compare ordered surviving object identities after reorder, then invoke a surviving action.
decoy: Compare sets of labels without checking order or identity.

situation: The palette tool accepts only opaque foreground/background pairs. A designer supplies a translucent overlay.
expected: Reject or mark outside policy rather than silently returning an opaque-pair ratio.
decoy: Discard the alpha channel before grading.

situation: A theme color resolves differently in light and dark appearance. Both audit reports have the same value.
expected: Resolve against each requested appearance and compare a known dynamic pair.
decoy: Read the machine's current appearance for both reports.

situation: A mid-gray sample produces an unexpected contrast ratio, although black and white look correct.
expected: Check transfer to linear luminance using a non-endpoint sample and an independent expected value.
decoy: Use gamma-encoded channels directly; test only black and white.

situation: The same intended color arrives through two different color spaces in a theme file.
expected: Convert to a supported common space before the luminance calculation and handle conversion failure.
decoy: Compare unconverted component arrays as though both were sRGB.

situation: A document changes between two Find Next operations; an old insertion index no longer refers to the same text.
expected: Resolve a valid start for the current search snapshot and check the next target after editing.
decoy: Clamp the old numeric index and assume it identifies the same match.

situation: A card offers Archive and Remove shortcuts. Both names appear correct but we need to know which operation runs.
expected: Check each installed action name together with the callback recipient and return value.
decoy: Compare only the displayed names.

situation: A repeated illustration in each result adds a stop before every result title. The title and actions still matter.
expected: Exclude only decorative content while keeping the title and actions independently available.
decoy: Hide the common parent to remove the illustration.

situation: A movie has ordinary Spanish audio and described English audio. A viewer requests described Spanish audio.
expected: Require both language and description on the same option; leave an established nonempty selection untouched on no match.
decoy: Pick the ordinary Spanish track as the closest available choice.

situation: The same price label is configured repeatedly at successively larger and smaller text sizes with a brand font.
expected: Scale from the original design font for the effective size, without cumulative scaling.
decoy: Scale the font already installed on the label each time.

situation: A button is moved outside its original shelf but is still attached elsewhere. An older callback is retained.
expected: Check current ownership/eligibility, not just any superview; preserve a live shelf action.
decoy: Allow the operation whenever the old button has a parent.

situation: The ordinary button is disabled after its shortcut is created. Someone invokes the retained shortcut anyway.
expected: Recheck permission at invocation; disabled path does not dispatch and enabled path still works.
decoy: Check permission only while constructing the shortcut.

situation: Restoring focus can synchronously open the next panel before the first completion unwinds.
expected: Finish consuming old state before invoking external callbacks; preserve the newly opened panel.
decoy: Clear shared presentation state after calling the external restoration handler.

situation: A close animation can be interrupted or cancelled before the panel has disappeared.
expected: Request restoration on the owning successful completion, not when close is requested.
decoy: Post once immediately and suppress the actual completion.

situation: A settings client writes the same toggle value twice, then writes its opposite.
expected: Deduplicate the side effect on repeated values without suppressing the actual transition.
decoy: Fire the callback on every setter invocation.

situation: A dismissal completion can be called twice by a test driver and once late after reopening.
expected: Only the first eligible completion for the active owner can request restoration.
decoy: Test two different sessions and never deliver the same completion twice.

situation: A refreshed tree has duplicate identifiers in separate branches. A valid previous tree is onscreen.
expected: Reject atomically across the whole input, preserving the previous tree.
decoy: Validate each sibling array separately as it is installed.

situation: An editor switches from writable to read-only while the menu remains visible.
expected: Update help and action eligibility together; retained obsolete commands cannot edit.
decoy: Remove the visible menu title but leave its command enabled.

situation: A document editor can group editing commands, but some customers leave that setting off.
expected: Use the SDK edit-category value only when requested, and preserve default category and handler otherwise.
decoy: Invent an edit enum case or force grouping in both configurations.

situation: Text is replaced through the native editor while a list of search matches is cached.
expected: Invalidate or recompute matches against the live document before navigation.
decoy: Invalidate matches only when the query string changes.

situation: The original focus target remains attached but refuses focus when the inspector closes.
expected: Resolve eligibility at completion and use an eligible fallback exactly once.
decoy: Assume that being attached makes the original target eligible.

situation: A component installs keyboard traversal links beside an existing route owned by another component.
expected: Preserve externally owned links while updating the component's own route.
decoy: Rebuild every traversal link through this component on each update.

situation: The selected subtitle translates only occasional dialogue; the menu is supposed to offer complete captions.
expected: Filter forced-only options from the offered full captions without treating an existing unlisted choice as Off.
decoy: Present every legible option as full captions.

situation: A query matches just part of a composed character; the editor must not expose a partial navigation target.
expected: Check candidate bounds against the actual string's character boundaries.
decoy: Accept any nonempty range inside the UTF-16 length.

situation: A native text field changes before validation returns, without going through the form's edit helper.
expected: Reject stale input through a live snapshot and release only that submission's busy state.
decoy: Assume every edit calls cancellation before the reply.

situation: Opening a read-only inventory races with someone choosing different audio in the player.
expected: Inspect groups and characteristics without selection writes, even after delayed results.
decoy: Restore the preinspection selections after the read finishes.

situation: A representable updates its underlying control from handler A to B and later tears down.
expected: Check old, current and retired registrations independently; preserve current ordinary dispatch.
decoy: Press only the current button after teardown.

situation: Some required fields are invalid when a user invokes Submit through an alternate input path.
expected: Validate before dispatch; retain meaningful field errors and permit a later valid submission.
decoy: Disable only the visual button and leave the handler unchecked.

situation: Keyboard navigation includes an invisible or disabled control between two usable controls.
expected: Resolve the next eligible target in the current hierarchy, including its ancestors.
decoy: Filter only on the control's own visible flag.

situation: A temporary panel disappears after installing keyboard traversal links into the surrounding view.
expected: Remove the links it owns or restore prior ones without breaking newer external links.
decoy: Set every next-key-view link to nil during teardown.

situation: Someone requests French audio on an asset with several languages. No exact eligible match may exist.
expected: Match the requested language according to declared policy and leave selection unchanged on failure.
decoy: Select the first audible option if no match is found.

situation: A media status panel has an indefinite duration but no explicit stream classification.
expected: Report the observed duration state without inferring that the asset is live.
decoy: Label all indefinite-duration items Live.

situation: A menu submits an identifier that is not present in the item's current options.
expected: Validate membership before changing either native or displayed selection.
decoy: Treat an unknown non-nil ID as Off.

situation: The background was already inaccessible for an unrelated reason before this panel opened.
expected: Snapshot and restore the prior accessibility state for the owning panel lifecycle.
decoy: Always restore the background to accessible.

situation: The low-motion version of a page drops information or a control that was present in the animated version.
expected: Preserve content, current selection and ordinary actions while changing motion.
decoy: Replace the animated content with an empty placeholder.

situation: The motion preference changes while the screen is alive, but its next transition uses stale settings.
expected: Observe the relevant preference and re-read it for the current owner.
decoy: Observe a different display preference because both affect appearance.

situation: A page transition should become immediate when Reduce Motion is selected. Content and page identity must stay the same.
expected: Use the effective preference and inspect the animation transaction before declaring a visual defect.
decoy: Add a substitute animation even where the product requires an immediate change.

situation: A localized item description wraps at large text sizes but its parent still reserves one line.
expected: Allow the label and containing layout to grow; protect the adjacent action.
decoy: Set numberOfLines without removing the conflicting single-line height.

situation: A change inside a screen and a transition to another screen need different accessibility requests.
expected: Select a request appropriate to the actual transition and distinguish the request from observed focus delivery.
decoy: Post a screen transition on every update.

situation: A notification was queued before the screen stopped observing and runs after a fresh subscription starts.
expected: Change the observed preference after restart; old queued work must be inert while new work still applies.
decoy: Check only that observation is currently active.

situation: A settings observer is stopped twice, then started again. The next change should refresh the view once.
expected: Unregister old tokens, keep teardown idempotent and establish one new registration.
decoy: Keep registering on each start and rely on identical output values.

situation: An earlier search navigation callback survives after the user changes the query.
expected: Bind navigation to the current query/document generation; preserve the current callback.
decoy: Use the newest match list from every previously installed closure.

situation: The player group forbids empty selection but a menu can still send Off.
expected: Respect the group's empty-selection policy and preserve current native selection on rejection.
decoy: Clear the group first and restore a display label if it fails.

situation: A primary button is configured with help text, then with no help text, without recreating the view.
expected: Clear the optional help on the same live button and preserve its action.
decoy: Retain the previous tooltip or substitute a semantically different empty value.

situation: The fast Save shortcut works. Someone reports that the adjacent ordinary Save button now opens the file instead.
expected: Trigger the actual ordinary controls as well as the installed shortcut and check each destination.
decoy: Validate only that a callback occurred.

situation: Searching for aa in aaa should expose different matches depending on the product's overlap setting.
expected: Check both policies with a string where overlapping and nonoverlapping ranges differ.
decoy: Use a sample where no matches overlap.

situation: A video screen restyles captions but must keep the player's normal playback controls.
expected: Preserve the existing player and built-in control configuration; separate metadata from playback policy.
decoy: Disable standard controls and substitute an accessibility-only action.

situation: An old menu still has a reference to the previous item's track group after replacing the player item.
expected: Validate group and owner against the live player item at dispatch.
decoy: Compare only a display name that exists on both items.

situation: A notification repeats without any effective preference change. A later genuinely different setting must still apply.
expected: Suppress duplicate effects, but let a changed current value through.
decoy: Count registration events rather than resulting state changes.

situation: A opens, B replaces it and then A finally finishes closing.
expected: Deliver A's installed callback after B opens; only B can restore once.
decoy: Read a shared current ticket when the old callback fires.

situation: Configuring selection on a reusable control must not discard an unrelated role or trait.
expected: Modify only owned trait bits and check both set and clear on the same object.
decoy: Replace the entire trait set on each selection update.

situation: A document contains an emoji before a search hit, and navigation selects the neighboring substring.
expected: Compare the actual selected substring with the query in the same document coordinate system.
decoy: Pass Swift Character counts as arbitrary native offsets.

situation: A player reports one buffered range and a different seekable range.
expected: Display each property with its actual meaning and preserve disjoint ranges.
decoy: Label buffered intervals as seekable destinations.

situation: A retained action is invoked after a row is configured again, even with the same record ID.
expected: Retire registrations by ownership, not ID alone, and prove the new action dispatches exactly once.
decoy: Test only rebinding to a different ID so lookup can mask stale dispatch.

situation: A setting is assigned its current value and then changed once.
expected: The change notification follows actual transitions; keep the declared return-value contract separate.
decoy: Use notification count as a proxy for the operation's success result.

situation: Validation finishes and a completion handler immediately submits new input.
expected: Consume old state before callback and avoid clearing the new active request afterward.
decoy: Reset a shared busy flag after external completion returns.

situation: A priority order cell becomes an ordinary order while it stays visible.
expected: Set the current name and status on the same instance and clear optional priority state only.
decoy: Clear the current order status along with the old priority wording.

situation: A deleted row's auxiliary control is still present in the programmatic navigation collection.
expected: Remove the old child from the exported collection without disturbing surviving controls.
decoy: Only detach it visually.

situation: The older of two reload requests returns last with a failure. Both use the same item.
expected: Keep the newest result and ownership; changing item ID is not required for supersession.
decoy: Key requests solely on the item's identifier.

situation: A user starts in the middle match and asks for previous rather than next.
expected: Resolve relative to the current target and requested direction with defined boundary behavior.
decoy: Always choose the first match or advance forward.

situation: A Mac list row reports selection and expansion and also contains an Open button.
expected: Preserve the native row role, current state and exposed independently actionable child.
decoy: Assume a parent reporting a role must hide every child.

situation: Selection moves from one result to another while both stay onscreen.
expected: Check both the old and new rows and preserve unrelated domain state.
decoy: Only mark the new row selected.

situation: A named accessibility command is visible but activating it does nothing.
expected: Invoke the installed command and verify its intended effect and success return.
decoy: Check names and presence but never invoke it.

situation: The playback-speed menu has localized titles, numeric rates and a currently active speed.
expected: Keep display metadata, rate and active choice distinct; do not infer one from menu order.
decoy: Treat the displayed label or first offered speed as the active rate.

situation: A list reorders while a record remains selected; later that record is removed.
expected: Keep selection by stable identity when it survives and clear it only when no longer eligible.
decoy: Keep the old index after reorder.

situation: A caption menu is refreshed and its old Off setter is retained by a client.
expected: Deliver that setter after a replacement choice is active; preserve the actual item selection and check a current Off.
decoy: Show only that the local picker ID did not change.

situation: Timeline values from the previous video remain visible while inspecting a new unavailable item.
expected: Invalidate old timeline state when the current item changes and distinguish missing data from a valid zero.
decoy: Keep the last nonempty result until a later successful load.

situation: An old outline node handle survives deletion, then a different node arrives using the same ID.
expected: Answer child queries only for live handles; removed nodes expose no stale children.
decoy: Resolve the old handle by ID and return the replacement's children.

situation: A merged table cell covers multiple row and column coordinates.
expected: Resolve each covered coordinate to the same cell and handle out-of-bounds requests safely.
decoy: Test only the merged cell's origin coordinate.

situation: A text preview changes size while the same label is onscreen and can later move back to the original size.
expected: Recompute using the actual owner of the size preference and preserve wrapping and the ordinary action.
decoy: Scale once from the initial trait or always follow ambient settings despite an explicit preview.

situation: The inspector opens before a clip exists, then receives an item without the requested group.
expected: Distinguish unavailable from inspected-empty and use comparisons that support the supplied payload types.
decoy: Return empty for both inputs or require invalid synthesized equality.

situation: A forced track is active but intentionally absent from the menu of complete captions.
expected: Represent the existing choice separately from Off and preserve it until the user selects another option.
decoy: Clear the player selection to make it agree with the filtered list.

situation: A field error is corrected without recreating the form.
expected: Replace or clear the relevant help/error state on the live field and leave other fields intact.
decoy: Leave stale instructions on the corrected field.

situation: Two TV buttons have different accessibility names but look blank to someone using the remote.
expected: Inspect actual visible titles for both controls, not testing identifiers or speech labels.
decoy: Set only the accessibility identifier.
